clue.text: A leg's an odd item on the menu

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange or irregular, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner is puzzled to find a leg listed as a peculiar menu dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked Italian pasta dish is a familiar choice on restaurant menus.

clue.text: Cat like Pope?

definitions.meaning: resembling a big cat such as a lion
relating to one of the popes named Leo

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lion-like, and also of or relating to a Pope Leo, as in the Leonine City.

clue.text: Able to see where it's said to be placed

indicators.note: said tells us the word meaning placed is heard rather than written

parts.note: something sited is placed or positioned somewhere

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether a thing can see where it is supposed to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sighted has working vision, the opposite of blind.

clue.text: King held singular character with scant hope

indicators.note: held means the royal abbreviation keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
singular means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A monarch possessed an odd personality that left little room for optimism.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doomed or past saving is informally called this; their chances are slim.

clue.text: Purse made former companion turn queer

parts.note: ex is a former partner, or simply means former
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: turn asks for the letters of the following word to be turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A one-time friend went strange and made off with a wallet.
explanation.definitionFit: The national treasury of Britain is its public purse, the funds the government spends.

clue.text: Rider rejected transvestite garments from old witch

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the clothing word is read from end to start

parts.note: drag is the clothing of one sex worn by the other

explanation.surface: A horseman turns down cross-dressing outfits handed over by an ancient crone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rider is not a horseman but H. Rider Haggard, the Victorian author of King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider is the middle name of the novelist H. Rider Haggard, so the first name defines the surname.

clue.text: Politician gets hot with fever

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
an ague is a malarial fever with shivering

explanation.surface: A member of parliament comes down with a temperature and fever.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague is a British Conservative politician, once party leader and Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific British politician, William Hague, leader of the Conservatives from 1997 to 2001.

clue.text: Plant cheerful with promises — about a pound

parts.note: glad means happy or cheerful

indicators.note: about means going round, so the promises surround the weight

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A happy gardener buys a flower on credit for about a quid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden flower with sword-shaped leaves, grown from corms.

clue.text: Tarmac orders snake to stop

parts.note: the asp is a venomous Egyptian snake
halt means stop

explanation.surface: Someone on the runway commands a serpent to come to a standstill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is a road surfacing material of tar and stones, much like this bitumen surfacing.

clue.text: Swell managed without a gun

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the verb wraps round the weapon

parts.note: did means managed, as in 'did well'
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone coped fine without carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense it means outside, so the verb wraps round the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand or bulge outward from internal pressure.

clue.text: Natural growth fostered by grain company

indicators.note: growth that is fostered develops into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business expands steadily, nurtured by its cereal crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally, without artificial chemicals.

clue.text: Puffer with little weight of matter

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
pus is the matter from an infected wound

explanation.surface: A smoker frets about a small amount of substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A grampus is a dolphin-like cetacean that blows audibly, so it puffs.

clue.text: Plead to dine out over monastic service

indicators.note: over means covering, so the rearranged meal word lies around the office
out means the letters of dine are put out of order

parts.note: terce is the monastic office said at the third hour

explanation.surface: Someone begs to go to a restaurant once the monks' prayers are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE into INDE; terce is one of the canonical hours of the monastic day.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead on behalf of another is to intervene or mediate for them.

clue.text: Hook loses head with anger

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter of the seafarer is dropped

parts.note: Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Captain Hook is beheaded and furious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious or cross is being filled with anger.

clue.text: Present letter to Jones

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
Dow goes before Jones in the Dow Jones stock index

explanation.surface: A gift note is written to someone called Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dow Jones is the American share index; DOW is what is put next to Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone with money or a gift is to bestow or endow it.

clue.text: Ash bin was upset, making this a necessity

definitions.text: Ash bin was upset, making this a necessity

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the first three words are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Knocking over the rubbish bin means you will need to wash your hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash basin is a sink for washing hands, needed after spilling an ash bin.

clue.text: It's strange, not being told

definitions.meaning: having no connection, alien to the matter
not recounted or narrated, taking related as meaning told

explanation.definitionFit: The word means having no connection, and punningly not related, that is not recounted as a story.

clue.text: One of them can go to the hole in the wall for part of 17 across

definitions.text: One of them can go to the hole in the wall for part of 17 across

parts.words: One of them can go to the hole in the wall for part of 17 across
parts.note: the hole in the wall suggests a cash machine, but these wall plugs fill drilled holes to hold screws

explanation.surface: Someone queues at a cashpoint to fund part of a project.
explanation.walkthrough: A hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine; here it is a literal drilled hole. Rawlplug is a trademark for wall plugs.
explanation.definitionFit: These fibre or plastic plugs are pushed into drilled holes in masonry to grip screws.

clue.text: Joiner of golfer's complement?

parts.note: woods are golf clubs, and Tiger Woods is a golfer
a ship's complement is its crew

explanation.surface: A carpenter belongs to a golfer's support team.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw for wood fastens or joins pieces of timber together.

clue.text: Dawn let loose about Romney?

indicators.note: letting loose and scattering about puts the letters of the two words into new order

explanation.surface: Dawn is turned loose to roam around a place called Romney.
explanation.walkthrough: Romney Marsh is a stretch of reclaimed marshland in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Romney Marsh is an example of marshy low-lying ground, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Is clout appropriate for treating the 2?

indicators.note: appropriate as a verb means taking over, so the letters are seized and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether hitting a patient is a suitable treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 2' points to 2 down, the clue about being able to see; this specialist looks after eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor is one who examines and treats people's vision.

clue.text: Revolutionary bears a weapon

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, so the letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An insurgent carries a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry sword with a curved blade is a type of weapon.

clue.text: Asian gets me in 4

indicators.note: in tells us the pronoun sits inside the purse word

parts.note: the clue at 4 down is defined as purse, and a burse is an old word for a purse

explanation.surface: An Asian ends up in the treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Myanmar, formerly Burma, in south-east Asia.

clue.text: Style — some present it less than others

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A remark that some people give a gift less often than others do.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a title, which is to entitle them.

clue.text: Some of the day a doctor is on hand

parts.note: THU, short for Thursday, is part of a day name
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor is available for part of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb is a digit found on every hand.

clue.text: Keep it under your hat!

parts.note: keeping something under your hat is the idiom for not revealing it

explanation.definitionFit: Highly classified information must be kept confidential, not disclosed.

clue.text: Piece of metal plate or cup elsewhere

definitions.meaning: a piece of plate armour protecting the thigh
the French word for a cup, so a cup abroad

explanation.definitionFit: It is a thigh plate in a suit of armour, and the French for cup.

clue.text: Nigel playing with marbles?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the name are played about with

explanation.surface: Nigel plays a game of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are classical Greek sculptures taken from the Parthenon, now in the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin's name goes with marbles in the famous sculptures' title.

clue.text: Various names turn sail into sea

indicators.note: turn means the letters of the two words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to steer a boat out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed or alternative names someone goes by are their pseudonyms.

clue.text: Ointment for a Frenchman round the bend?

indicators.note: round means the man wraps around the bend

parts.note: un is French for a, and a gent is a man
a U-bend gives U

explanation.surface: Some cream for a man from France who has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' is slang for mad, but here U, a U-bend, goes inside UN GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing salve or cream applied to the skin.

clue.text: Relief with mid-river shelter

indicators.note: mid means in the middle of, so the shelter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: Respite comes from a hut set up in the middle of a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: An easing of tension between nations, especially in the Cold War, is a relief.

clue.text: Genuine, because given religious education

parts.note: since means because
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A believer is earnest because of their religious schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being genuine means being honest and heartfelt in what you say.
